title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes build an axiomatic framework for tame ('modérée') topology. The basic object is a 'magma' of figures: a set M of figures (for example piecewise-linear or semi-algebraic subsets) carrying structure relations. These are ≤ (inclusion), a strict or 'interior' inclusion written ≤ with a small circle (later ≪), a disjointness or separation relation |·|, and derived relations after the '//' (a crossed relation, apparently non-inclusion ≰ or 'meets', and ∥). The surrounding pages ask which maps between such structures count as homomorphisms. Example 1 (previous page) covers pullbacks f* of figures, which turn a 'multiplicity' into an isomorphism or into ∅. Example 2 is the product map F ↦ F×F'.

This page, Example 3, takes the case of passing from a tame class (modération) M to a sub-class M', or from a magma to a sub-magma. This is in the spirit of restricting the type of tameness. One keeps only figures with extra properties: connectedness or irreducibility, regularity, being 'bien liés', or being 'simplexes' in a more or less strong sense. These sub-classes should still be numerous enough that everything reduces to M', notably through affine M'-subdivisions. The model case is that every polyhedron is a finite union of simplices, as in triangulation or cell decomposition.

The claim: for the inclusion M' → M, all the structures ≤, ≤°, |·| and the derived ones are preserved, except possibly ≤°. That relation may have to be replaced by a relative version ≤°_rel, defined intrinsically inside M'. Consequently the derived relation built from it must also be replaced by its relative version. So this is a magma homomorphism that is an embedding, and it raises none of the difficulties met in Example 1.

The next page makes this precise. M' is required to be closed in (M, ≤), and a convexity condition is imposed: if X ≪ Y' ≤ Y with X, Y in M', then Y' lies in M'. Under that condition ≪_{M'} equals the restriction ≪_M|M', and the axioms Mag 1–4 pass to M'.
errors: No mathematical error. The only subtlety is the one Grothendieck flags himself: an interior-type relation defined intrinsically in a sub-class need not equal the restriction of the ambient relation. This is resolved on the next page by the convexity hypothesis b).

ideas.what: Restricting a tame class of figures to a generating sub-class (connected, irreducible, regular, simplices) that still reaches everything via affine subdivisions
ideas.modern_name: Cell decomposition / triangulation in o-minimal or semi-algebraic geometry; generating sub-classes of a tame structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn (o-minimal cell decomposition, 1980s); Łojasiewicz and Hironaka (semi-algebraic triangulation)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) §5–6 calls for a 'topologie modérée' but without this axiomatics

ideas.what: Sub-magma inclusion as an embedding-type homomorphism preserving the order and disjointness relations, with interior inclusion possibly replaced by a relative version
ideas.modern_name: Embedding of relational structures; induced versus intrinsic relations; a convexity condition ensuring the induced relation is intrinsic
ideas.where_published: Only in these Analysis situs manuscripts (cote 156)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine step in an unpublished axiomatic program for tame topology: checking that sub-classes give sub-magmas. The broader program is of historical interest, but this page contains no non-trivial result or connection that is absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 likely reads 'sous-modération, ou d'un magma M à un sous-magma M'' (the M and M' are superscripts over 'magma'), rather than 'modération' twice.
'restrictions de type de modération' likely 'restrictions du type de modérations'.
'mais que [-restent-] {+passent+} non bornées' more plausibly 'mais qui [-restent-] sont assez nombreuses pour "se réduire à M'"'; 'vis-à-vis' is likely 'via'.
'Dans un tel cas, seulement on remarquera' probably 'Dans un tel cas, visiblement on remarquera'.
'notion de [?] modération, qui est une flagrante' probably 'notion d'homomorphisme de magmas, qui est un plongement'.
'des types de celles évoquées avec les exemples 1' probably 'du type de celles évoquées avec les exemples 1'.
